The *Itodinnakathā* is a debate section preserved in the seventh chapter of the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 7.6) within the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. According to SuttaCentral, the text is associated with the *Puttasutta* (AN 5.39) and the *Tirokuṭṭa Sutta* (Kp 7 / PTS Kp 6), and is currently represented by one translation in a modern language [SuttaCentral].
Textual reuse analysis by DharmaNexus documents 43 matching passages across six other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Concordant with the cross-reference noted by SuttaCentral, the most extensive text reuse occurs with the *Pañcakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 5.39), with its longest shared passage spanning segments §9.5–14.4 of Kv 7.6 and §39.1.1–39.6.4 of AN 5 [DharmaNexus]. Further phrase-level parallels within the *Kathāvatthu* occur in the *Puggalakathā* (Kv 1.1) and the *Dānakathā* (Kv 7.4) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also finds shared passages in the commentary *Khuddakapāṭha-aṭṭhakathā* and later anthological or question-and-answer texts such as the *Kavidappaṇanīti* and the *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā Aṅguttaranikāye* [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, automated alignments identify low-plausibility matches with the Chinese *Ekottarika-āgama* (T 125) [DharmaNexus].
